In [[abstract algebra]], particularly [[ring theory]], '''maximal common divisors''' are an abstraction of the [[number theory]] concept of [[greatest common divisor]] (GCD). This definition is slightly more general than GCDs, and may exist in rings in which GCDs do not. Halter-Koch (1998) provides the following definition.<ref name="Ideal Systems">{{cite book|title=Ideal systems|publisher=Marcel Dekker|first=Franz|last=Halter-Koch|year=1998|isbn=0-8247-0186-0}}</ref>

<math> d\in H</math> is a maximal common divisor of a subset, <math> B\subset H</math> , if the following criteria are met:
# <math> d|b </math>  for all <math> b\in B</math>
# Suppose <math> c\in H</math>, <math> d|c</math> and <math> c|b </math>  for all <math> b\in B</math>. Then <math>c \simeq d</math>.
